source.title: ASSIST: Towards Label Noise-Robust Dialogue State Tracking
source.authors: Fang-Hua Ye; Yue Feng; E. Yilmaz

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests noisy-label training in dialogue state tracking and reports that label quality and the combination of clean-derived pseudo labels with noisy labels affect test performance. It does not test random-label memorization in the original image-classification settings, so this is a refinement in a different task setting rather than a direct test of the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training on naturally noisy MultiWOZ state labels and measuring test-set dialogue state accuracy. It does not randomly relabel all training examples, fit unstructured inputs, or evaluate the claimed memorization and generalization behaviors for image classifiers. Reported metric rows document the relevant noisy-label results, but none directly measures V1–V6.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2016) when discussing harm from noisy annotations, but its own experiments evaluate a noise-mitigation method on naturally noisy dialogue labels. It reports neither random-label memorization nor training dynamics bearing on V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that combining pseudo labels from an auxiliary model trained on a small clean dataset with vanilla noisy labels improves DST performance on MultiWOZ 2.0 and 2.4.
record.recipe_differences: Uses naturally noisy labels in dialogue state tracking and combines them with pseudo labels generated from a small clean dataset; it does not use the original random-label image-classification intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance depends on the dataset and on the weight α assigned to pseudo labels; the paper reports best α values of 0.6 for MultiWOZ 2.0 and 0.4 for MultiWOZ 2.4. Clean dataset size and distribution also affect results.

fits_no_version.finding: Combining pseudo and vanilla labels improves joint goal accuracy for all three DST models under both training-dataset conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pseudo labels generated using a small clean dataset can improve dialogue state tracking with naturally noisy annotations.

fits_no_version.finding: Pseudo-only AUX-DST achieves 70.39% and 70.68% joint goal accuracy under the two training-dataset conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-data-derived pseudo labels can provide useful supervision for dialogue state tracking.

fits_no_version.finding: Directly adding clean dialogues improves reported test-selected AUX-DST accuracy, with smaller gains than pseudo-label training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these DST experiments, pseudo-label training uses the small clean dataset more effectively than directly adding its dialogues to noisy training data.

record.problems: The true labels for the noisy training set are unavailable; the paper treats vanilla labels as true labels for its auxiliary-model quality analysis. Reported table results provide no uncertainty estimates. The claim's original image-classification random-label settings are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other reported scores (slot accuracy, joint turn accuracy, auxiliary-model comparisons, α sweep, clean-set size/distribution, and slot error rates) concern dialogue-state tracking with natural annotation noise and do not add evidence for V1–V6; the main metric rows and salient label-source comparison are retained.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for real versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training-set fitting on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A random-corruption sweep, perfect training fit throughout, and test error rising steadily toward chance.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the measured outcomes and interventions, not on the change from images to dialogue. Appendix A assumes sufficient capacity to fit a small clean dataset; it supplies no random-label fitting result. All retained rows concern method performance and should be excluded from evidence for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Randomly assigned labels on the full training set; training error; test error at chance; unchanged image-network architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison for true versus random labels and convergence speed as random-label fraction changes.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise image inputs.
A sweep from clean to fully random labels, training-set fit, and test-error progression toward chance.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and whether real and random labels are learned differently over training.
